latest_apis.rationale: Async request APIs, app-router conventions and navigation APIs are all current, but the caching/navigation model is the outgoing one: Next.js 16.4 (Oct 2026) recommends Cache Components for every app and it becomes the default in 17, under which `dynamic`, hand-rolled caches and prefetch opt-outs are all replaced (nextjs.org/blog/next-16-4; docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).

churn_resistance.rationale: Data access and typing are genuinely well-isolated, but the framework's own active churn area (caching model, prefetching, Suspense shells) is exactly where this app will need edits across layout, every page and 8 link sites when Next 17 defaults Cache Components.

findings.issue: App-wide `dynamic = "force-dynamic"` keeps the whole app on the previous rendering model; Next 16.4 now recommends Cache Components for every app (default in create-next-app, default in Next 17), where route segment configs are removed and replaced by `use cache`/`cacheLife` + Suspense shells.
findings.suggestion: Enable cacheComponents and express "live data" with uncached fetches inside Suspense boundaries (or `use cache` + `cacheLife` where caching is wanted), removing the segment config.

findings.issue: Blanket `prefetch={false}` (8 sites: PokemonCards.tsx:11, MoveTable.tsx:103, TypeBadge.tsx:17, page.tsx:69/77, pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:121/168, types/[name]/page.tsx:75) disables the App-Shell prefetch that Partial Prefetching (16.3/16.4) makes cheap and default, so navigations will stay slow after the framework's intended upgrade.
findings.suggestion: Drop `prefetch={false}` and let default App Shell prefetching work; opt-in per-link `prefetch` only where URL-specific prefetch is wanted.

findings.issue: No loading.tsx or Suspense boundary on any route: every page blocks on the full API fetch chain before first paint, and the recommended Cache Components model requires Suspense boundaries around runtime data — meaning per-page edits at migration time.
findings.suggestion: Stream pages with loading.tsx or Suspense-wrapped data components so a static shell renders immediately.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled 5,000-entry Map cache with TTL re-implements framework caching; under the recommended model `use cache` + `cacheLife({ revalidate: 60 })`/`cacheTag` provides this declaratively (and `unstable_cache`, the previous-model option, is deprecated in 16).
findings.suggestion: Replace the Map cache with `use cache` functions or fetch-level caching so eviction/TTL semantics track the framework's.

findings.issue: Raw `` with `@next/next/no-img-element` suppressed instead of `next/image`, bypassing the framework's image optimization primitive (second site: PokemonCards.tsx:12).
findings.suggestion: Use next/image with `remotePatterns` derived from API_BASE_URL in next.config.ts, or keep raw but document the deliberate tradeoff.

findings.issue: `turbopack: { root: __dirname }` — bare `__dirname` is documented as fragile (undefined under ESM configs; see vercel/next.js issue #92540, vercel#16405).
findings.suggestion: Use `path.join(__dirname)` / `import.meta.dirname` with a fallback, or hard-code/derive the root from process.cwd().

findings.issue: Hand-rolled `Params`/`SearchParams` prop types on every page instead of Next 15.5+/16 generated route types (`PageProps<'/pokemon/[name]'>`), which keep types in sync with the actual route tree.
findings.suggestion: Enable typed routes and use the generated PageProps/LayoutProps helpers.

findings.issue: @types/node ^20 while the environment is Node 24; minor drift.

summary: A lean, well-typed app with an exemplary single data-access boundary and zero wasteful dependencies, using current request/navigation APIs throughout. But it is built squarely on Next's outgoing caching model — force-dynamic, a hand-rolled cache, blanket prefetch={false} and no Suspense boundaries — precisely where the framework is heading next (16.4 recommends Cache Components for every app; Next 17 makes it the default), so the Next 17 upgrade touches many files. Acceptable and unremarkable today, with a known migration bill attached.

apis.replacement: Cache Components: remove segment config; use `use cache`/`cacheLife` + Suspense boundaries (docs: migrating-to-cache-components; deprecated only under cacheComponents, removed when it becomes default in 17)
Default App-Shell prefetch under Partial Prefetching (16.3+); per-link prefetch for URL-specific content
